_comment: Rulebook: the laws, regulations and standards the organizations on the map operate under, by domain. Built to HELP (what meeting each rule well looks like), not only to flag. Plain-language summaries are general information, not legal advice; the linked official text governs. Each link is opened and checked by src/maintenance/rulebook.py, which stamps the date.

conflicts_of_interest.definition: A conflict of interest exists when someone who owes a duty to act for others (shareholders, the public, a client, a charity) has a personal or outside interest that could influence, or reasonably appear to influence, their judgment.
conflicts_of_interest.principle: Having a conflict is not wrongdoing; failing to disclose and manage it is.

degrees.actual: the interest is present when a decision is made
degrees.potential: it could arise from current interests
degrees.perceived: a reasonable person would suspect it (ethics codes treat appearance seriously too)

fixes: Independent approval by people without the conflict
Publish the policy and how it was applied

types.example: Owning shares in, or being paid by, the other side
Sitting on two boards, or on both sides of one deal
A relative on the other side

types.visible: only for officials who must report them

types.example: The company doing business with its own insiders
types.visible: only when disclosed (proxy Item 404, Form 990 Schedule L)

types.example: Regulator to regulated; lawmaker to lobbyist or board
types.visible: yes: Congress records, lobbying disclosures, board filings

types.example: A firm whose business lines pull against each other (e.g. writing requirements and then bidding)
The same investor holding large stakes in competitors

domains.DOM_C: Sovereign Statecraft, Central Banking & Institutional Capital
domains.DOM_E: Life Sciences, Public Health & Biotech Capital
domains.INTL: International (applies to foreign or multinational organizations)

rules.name: Securities Act of 1933
rules.requires: Truthful registration and disclosure when securities are offered to the public.
rules.helps: Plain, complete offering documents; disclose risks and related parties up front.

rules.name: Securities Exchange Act §16(a): insider reporting
rules.requires: Directors, officers and 10%+ owners of public companies report their holdings and trades (Forms 3, 4, 5).
rules.helps: File on time; keep a board calendar for filing deadlines; the public record then speaks for itself.

rules.name: Securities Exchange Act §13(d): 5% ownership disclosure
rules.requires: Anyone acquiring more than 5% of a class of voting shares files Schedule 13D or 13G.
rules.helps: Timely, accurate ownership filings make concentration visible and reduce surprise control shifts.

rules.name: Regulation S-K Item 404: related-person transactions
rules.requires: Public companies disclose transactions over $120,000 with directors, officers, 5% holders and their families, and their approval policy.
rules.helps: Adopt a written related-party policy, have independent directors approve each transaction, disclose it clearly.

rules.name: Regulation S-K Item 407: board independence and committees
rules.requires: Disclose which directors are independent, committee composition, and compensation-committee interlocks.
rules.helps: Explain each independence judgment; rotate committee chairs; disclose interlocks even when allowed.

rules.name: Sarbanes-Oxley Act: certifications, internal controls, audit committees, whistleblowers
rules.requires: CEO/CFO certify reports; companies maintain internal controls; audit committees are independent; employees who report fraud are protected.
rules.helps: A real, independent audit committee and a protected, well-publicized internal reporting channel.

rules.name: NYSE 303A.01 / Nasdaq 5605(b): majority-independent boards
rules.citation: NYSE Listed Company Manual 303A.01; Nasdaq Rule 5605(b)(1)
rules.requires: A majority of the board must be independent (controlled companies are exempt).
rules.helps: Go beyond the minimum: independent chair or lead director, regular executive sessions without management.

rules.name: Clayton Act §8: interlocking directorates
rules.requires: The same person may not serve as director or officer of two competing corporations above size thresholds.
rules.helps: Screen every new board seat against competitors before accepting it; document the review.

rules.name: Sherman Act
rules.requires: No agreements that restrain trade; no monopolization.
rules.helps: Antitrust training for executives and directors who sit on multiple boards or trade associations.

rules.name: Clayton Act §7 and Hart-Scott-Rodino premerger notice
rules.requires: Mergers that may substantially lessen competition are prohibited; large deals are notified in advance.
rules.helps: Assess concentration (HHI) before deals and publish the competitive rationale.

rules.name: DOJ/FTC Merger Guidelines (2023)
rules.requires: Explains how the agencies assess concentration; HHI above 1,800 marks a highly concentrated market.
rules.helps: Use the same yardstick internally when evaluating acquisitions.

rules.name: FTC Act §5: unfair or deceptive practices
rules.requires: No unfair methods of competition or deceptive acts toward consumers.
rules.helps: Substantiate marketing claims; plain-language terms and pricing.

rules.name: Foreign Corrupt Practices Act
rules.requires: No bribes to foreign officials; accurate books and records and internal accounting controls.
rules.helps: Third-party due diligence on foreign agents and joint-venture partners; gifts and hospitality register.

rules.name: False Claims Act
rules.regulator: DOJ Civil Division; qui tam relators
rules.requires: No knowingly false claims for government money; liability for damages and penalties; whistleblower (qui tam) suits.
rules.helps: Compliance programs for billing and contracting; prompt self-disclosure and repayment of overpayments.

rules.name: Lobbying Disclosure Act
rules.regulator: Secretary of the Senate; Clerk of the House
rules.requires: Lobbyists register and report clients, issues, spending and their former government positions.
rules.helps: Publish your own lobbying positions and spending on your website, beyond the legal minimum.

rules.name: Foreign Agents Registration Act
rules.requires: People acting in the U.S. for foreign governments, parties or companies register and disclose the work.
rules.helps: Screen engagements for foreign principals; register when in doubt; label informational materials.

rules.name: Federal Election Campaign Act (incl. corporate contribution ban)
rules.requires: Corporations may not contribute directly to federal candidates; they may sponsor PACs that report all receipts and contributions.
rules.helps: Publish a political-spending policy and board oversight of it (a common shareholder request).

rules.name: Post-government employment restrictions
rules.regulator: DOJ; Office of Government Ethics; Senate Ethics
rules.requires: Former officials, including Senators and senior staff, face cooling-off periods before lobbying their former colleagues.
rules.helps: Check cooling-off periods before hiring former officials; publish who you hired and when.

rules.name: Executive-branch financial conflicts of interest
rules.requires: Executive-branch employees may not act on matters affecting their own financial interests.
rules.helps: Recusal and divestment plans published at confirmation.

rules.name: Ethics in Government Act / STOCK Act: financial disclosure
rules.regulator: Senate Select Committee on Ethics; Office of Government Ethics
rules.requires: Members of Congress and senior officials file annual financial disclosures and periodic transaction reports.
rules.helps: Officials can post disclosures and recusals proactively in plain language.

rules.name: Sanctions (IEEPA and OFAC regulations)
rules.citation: 50 U.S.C. §1701 et seq.; 31 CFR Chapter V
rules.requires: No dealings with sanctioned persons, entities or countries without a license.
rules.helps: Screen counterparties and owners (50% rule) continuously, not only at onboarding.

rules.name: CFIUS foreign-investment review (FIRRMA)
rules.regulator: Committee on Foreign Investment in the U.S. (Treasury chair)
rules.requires: Foreign investments in U.S. businesses touching critical technology, infrastructure or data may need review.
rules.helps: Map foreign ownership (GLEIF parents) early; file voluntarily when unsure.

rules.name: Bank Secrecy Act; Corporate Transparency Act (beneficial ownership)
rules.requires: Anti-money-laundering programs at financial institutions; beneficial-ownership reporting (scope narrowed for U.S. companies by FinCEN in 2025: check the current rule).
rules.helps: Know and publish who ultimately owns and controls the organization.

rules.name: Tax-exempt organizations: exemption, excess benefit, annual return
rules.requires: Charities serve public purposes, avoid excess benefits to insiders, and file Form 990 (governance policies in Part VI).
rules.helps: Adopt and enforce a conflict-of-interest policy, whistleblower and document-retention policies (990 Part VI lines 12–14).

rules.name: ISS U.S. Proxy Voting Guidelines: director commitments
rules.citation: ISS U.S. Proxy Voting Guidelines (board composition)
rules.requires: Generally opposes directors on more than five public boards, or CEOs on more than two outside boards.
rules.helps: Set and publish a board-commitments policy.

rules.name: UK Corporate Governance Code: independence and tenure
rules.requires: More than nine years on a board is a circumstance likely to impair independence; companies explain if they differ.
rules.helps: Board refreshment plans; succession for long-serving directors.

rules.name: Federal Acquisition Regulation
rules.requires: Rules for federal contracting, including contractor ethics codes and mandatory disclosure of credible evidence of fraud (FAR 52.203-13).
rules.helps: A written contractor code of business ethics, internal control system and hotline.

rules.name: Procurement Integrity Act
rules.requires: Limits on disclosing bid information and on former procurement officials taking compensation from contractors.
rules.helps: Screen hires who were government procurement officials; keep records of the screening.

rules.name: DFARS safeguarding covered defense information; CMMC
rules.requires: Defense contractors protect controlled unclassified information (NIST SP 800-171) and report cyber incidents; CMMC certification levels.
rules.helps: Implement NIST SP 800-171 fully and honestly score it; most FCA cyber cases begin with overstated scores.

rules.name: Truthful Cost or Pricing Data (TINA)
rules.requires: Contractors certify that cost or pricing data are accurate, complete and current.
rules.helps: Disclose all pricing data, including unfavorable data; keep a certification file.

rules.name: Export controls (Arms Export Control Act/ITAR; Export Control Reform Act/EAR)
rules.requires: Licenses for exporting defense articles and controlled dual-use technology, including chips and AI hardware.
rules.helps: Classify products, screen end users, voluntary self-disclosure of mistakes.

rules.name: Defense Production Act
rules.requires: Government can prioritize contracts and fund industrial-base capacity in national-defense needs.
rules.helps: Transparent reporting of DPA awards and conditions.

rules.name: Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act
rules.requires: Food, drugs, devices and cosmetics must be safe and truthfully labeled; drugs and devices approved or cleared before marketing; no off-label promotion.
rules.helps: Promotion reviewed against the approved label; publish clinical results.

rules.name: FDA Food Safety Modernization Act
rules.requires: Food facilities run hazard analysis and preventive controls; supplier verification.
rules.helps: Supplier verification programs that reach smallholder and overseas suppliers.

rules.name: Federal Meat Inspection Act; Packers and Stockyards Act
rules.citation: 21 U.S.C. §601 et seq.; 7 U.S.C. §181 et seq.
rules.requires: Meat inspection; fair dealing toward livestock producers and growers.
rules.helps: Transparent contract terms for growers; publish grower payment methods.

rules.name: Robinson-Patman Act: price discrimination
rules.requires: Sellers may not discriminate in price between competing purchasers where it harms competition.
rules.helps: Document cost justifications for different pricing to large vs small retailers.

rules.name: Consumer Product Safety Act
rules.requires: Report product hazards promptly; recalls; safety standards.
rules.helps: Fast, public recall communication; report early.

rules.name: Fair Labor Standards Act
rules.requires: Minimum wage, overtime, child-labor limits.
rules.helps: Audit supply-chain labor practices, including contractors and franchisees.

rules.name: Federal Reserve Act
rules.requires: Structure and governance of the Federal Reserve System, including Reserve Bank director classes and Senate confirmation of Governors.
rules.helps: Publish Reserve Bank directors' affiliations and recusals.

rules.name: Bank Holding Company Act; Volcker Rule
rules.requires: Supervision of bank holding companies; limits on proprietary trading and fund ownership by banks.
rules.helps: Clear public reporting of fund interests and conflicts.

rules.name: Depository Institution Management Interlocks Act
rules.requires: Limits management officials serving at unaffiliated banks in the same area or above size thresholds.
rules.helps: Screen bank director appointments against other financial-institution seats.

rules.name: Investment Advisers Act; Investment Company Act
rules.requires: Fiduciary duty of advisers to clients; fund boards with independent directors; conflict disclosure.
rules.helps: Disclose stewardship and voting of large stakes (common-ownership transparency).

rules.name: Communications Act (incl. foreign ownership limits)
rules.requires: Licensing of broadcast and wireless; limits and review of foreign ownership of licensees.
rules.helps: Disclose ultimate ownership of licensees.

rules.name: FCC broadcast ownership rules
rules.requires: Limits on owning multiple broadcast stations in one market.
rules.helps: Public reporting of local station ownership and shared-services agreements.

rules.name: Sponsorship identification
rules.requires: Broadcast content paid for by someone must disclose the sponsor.
rules.helps: Apply the same disclosure to online and podcast content.

rules.name: Online platforms: Section 230; Children's Online Privacy Protection Act
rules.requires: Platform liability rules; parental consent for collecting children's data.
rules.helps: Age-appropriate design; publish moderation and data practices.

rules.name: CHIPS Act national-security guardrails
rules.requires: Recipients of chip subsidies limit expansion in countries of concern for ten years.
rules.helps: Publish award conditions and compliance reporting.

rules.name: EU GDPR, Digital Markets Act, Digital Services Act, AI Act
rules.requires: Data protection; gatekeeper obligations; platform transparency; risk-based AI rules.
rules.helps: Apply the strongest standard globally rather than region by region.

rules.name: NIST AI Risk Management Framework 1.0
rules.requires: Voluntary practices to govern, map, measure and manage AI risks.
rules.helps: Publish an AI risk profile using the framework.

rules.name: Anti-Kickback Statute
rules.requires: No payments to induce referrals or purchases paid by federal health programs.
rules.helps: Fair-market-value reviews of speaker fees and consulting; use OIG safe harbors and advisory opinions.

rules.name: Physician Self-Referral Law (Stark)
rules.requires: Physicians may not refer Medicare patients to entities they have financial relationships with, absent an exception.
rules.helps: Track physician financial relationships centrally; self-disclose problems.

rules.name: Physician Payments Sunshine Act (Open Payments)
rules.requires: Drug and device makers publicly report payments to physicians and teaching hospitals.
rules.helps: Report completely and early; explain payment purposes.

rules.name: Exclusion from federal health programs; civil monetary penalties
rules.requires: Excluded individuals and entities may not be paid by federal health programs, directly or indirectly.
rules.helps: Screen staff and vendors monthly against the exclusion list.

rules.name: Research financial conflicts of interest (PHS-funded research)
rules.citation: 42 CFR Part 50, Subpart F; 45 CFR Part 94
rules.requires: Institutions identify, manage and publicly report investigators' significant financial interests.
rules.helps: Publish investigator conflicts on a public page, as the rule allows.

rules.name: Bayh-Dole Act: federally funded inventions
rules.requires: Contractors may own inventions from federal funding but must disclose them; government keeps a license and march-in rights.
rules.helps: Disclose federal funding on patents and price commitments for publicly funded products.

rules.name: HIPAA privacy and security
rules.requires: Protect individually identifiable health information; breach notification.
rules.helps: Data minimization; prompt, plain breach notices.

rules.name: Protection of human research subjects (Common Rule)
rules.requires: Informed consent and independent ethics (IRB) review of federally funded human research.
rules.helps: Plain-language consent; publish results for every trial.

rules.name: Clean Air Act; Clean Water Act
rules.citation: 42 U.S.C. §7401 et seq.; 33 U.S.C. §1251 et seq.
rules.requires: Emission and discharge permits, monitoring and reporting.
rules.helps: Publish facility-level monitoring data and permit compliance.

rules.name: Superfund (CERCLA); hazardous waste (RCRA)
rules.requires: Liability for cleanup of hazardous releases; cradle-to-grave waste management.
rules.helps: Disclose legacy contamination liabilities and cleanup progress.

rules.name: Toxic Substances Control Act
rules.requires: Chemical reporting, testing and risk evaluation.
rules.helps: Report substantial-risk information promptly (TSCA §8(e)).

rules.name: Emergency Planning and Community Right-to-Know Act (Toxics Release Inventory)
rules.requires: Facilities report releases of listed toxic chemicals to the public inventory.
rules.helps: Community-facing summaries of each facility's releases.

rules.name: Occupational Safety and Health Act; Process Safety Management
rules.requires: Safe workplaces; process-safety programs at facilities with highly hazardous chemicals.
rules.helps: Publish incident rates and process-safety audits.

rules.name: Natural Gas Act; Federal Power Act
rules.citation: 15 U.S.C. §717 et seq.; 16 U.S.C. §791a et seq.
rules.requires: Federal regulation of interstate pipelines, LNG and wholesale power; just and reasonable rates; market-manipulation bans.
rules.helps: Transparent rate filings and affiliate-transaction disclosure.

rules.name: National Environmental Policy Act
rules.requires: Federal agencies assess environmental effects of major actions they fund or permit.
rules.helps: Early, honest community engagement on projects.

rules.name: Interested-director transactions (Delaware)
rules.regulator: Delaware courts (most large U.S. companies are Delaware corporations)
rules.requires: A deal in which a director or officer has an interest is protected only if it was disclosed and approved by disinterested directors or shareholders, or is fair to the company.
rules.helps: Disclose the interest in writing, leave the room for the vote, record the independent approval.

rules.name: Director's conflicting-interest transactions (Model Business Corporation Act)
rules.requires: Defines a director's conflicting interest (including relatives' interests) and the disclosure and qualified-director approval that make such a transaction valid.
rules.helps: Use the qualified-director approval process every time, even for small transactions.

rules.name: Standards of ethical conduct for executive-branch employees
rules.coi: Financial interest; gifts; outside jobs; impartiality; revolving door
rules.requires: Rules on gifts, financial conflicts, impartiality toward former employers and relatives, seeking future employment, and misuse of position.
rules.helps: Publish ethics agreements and recusal lists; screen meetings against them.

rules.name: Senate conflict-of-interest rule
rules.citation: Standing Rules of the Senate, Rule XXXVII
rules.coi: Financial interest; outside jobs; revolving door
rules.requires: Senators and staff may not use office for personal gain; limits on outside earned income, board service and negotiating future employment.
rules.helps: Post recusals and employment negotiations publicly, as the rule requires in some cases.

rules.name: House Code of Official Conduct
rules.citation: Rules of the House of Representatives, Rule XXIII
rules.requires: Members and staff conduct themselves to reflect credit on the House; limits on outside income, board service and use of office.
rules.helps: Publish stock-trading and recusal policies voluntarily.

rules.name: Organizational and consultant conflicts of interest (federal contracting)
rules.requires: Contracting officers identify and avoid, neutralize or mitigate conflicts such as a firm writing specifications and then bidding, or evaluating its own products.
rules.helps: Firewalls between business units; disclose potential conflicts in every proposal.

rules.name: Auditor independence
rules.requires: Auditors may not have financial, employment or business relationships with audit clients that impair independence.
rules.helps: Rotate audit partners; publish non-audit fees and why they don't impair independence.

rules.name: Lawyers: conflict of interest with current clients
rules.citation: ABA Model Rule of Professional Conduct 1.7 (adopted by most states)
rules.requires: A lawyer may not represent a client whose interests are directly adverse to another client, or materially limited by the lawyer's own interests, without informed written consent.
rules.helps: Run conflict checks before every new matter; get written consent.

rules.name: UK Bribery Act 2010
rules.requires: Offences for bribing and being bribed, and for companies failing to prevent bribery.
rules.helps: 'Adequate procedures' defense: risk assessment, due diligence, training, monitoring.

rules.name: UK Companies Act 2006, s.172: directors' duty to promote success (stakeholders)
rules.requires: Directors consider employees, suppliers, customers, community and environment, and report how they did (s.172 statement).
rules.helps: Make the s.172 statement specific and measurable.

rules.name: OECD Anti-Bribery Convention
rules.citation: OECD Convention on Combating Bribery of Foreign Public Officials (1997)
rules.regulator: OECD Working Group on Bribery (peer review)
rules.requires: Signatory countries criminalize bribery of foreign public officials.
rules.helps: Hold the same standard in every country of operation.
